saints.name: The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Forty soldiers of a Roman legion who were left to freeze on a frozen lake near Sebaste rather than deny Christ…
biography: About the year 320, in the persecution under the Emperor Licinius, forty Christian soldiers of the Twelfth Legion, the Fulminata, garrisoned at Sebaste in Lesser Armenia, refused to offer sacrifice and were condemned to freeze, stripped naked through a bitter night on a frozen pond outside the city.

A warm bath was set on the shore as the price of apostasy. One of the forty broke and ran to it, dying as he entered the water; but a guard named Aglaius, watching from the bank, saw crowns descending upon the martyrs, confessed himself a Christian, and stripped to take the apostate's place, so that the number forty stood complete.

At dawn the stiffened bodies, some still breathing, were burned and the ashes cast into a river, yet Christians gathered the relics and spread them through many cities. Basil of Caesarea preached their praise within living memory of their death, and Gregory of Nyssa, who buried his own parents beside their shrine, left two homilies in their honor.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 10 March
